setlist.title: Going Down The Road Feeling Bad jam

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): Reviewer highlights the sequence of Cryptical, Drums, The Other One, then Not Fade Away as top-notch 1970 Dead [7]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer calls The Other One fierce and rewarding on repeated listens [14]
- **Going Down The Road Feeling Bad jam** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the earliest Going Down The Road they could find: chords and solo, no vocals, after Good Lovin' [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **Casey Jones**: with false start [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-10-10.144636.sony-f95.lee.hance.sirmick.flac1648** (recommended): source not stated; 16 songs; 102 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: This copy is an upgrade over earlier circulating versions of the show [14]
- **gd70-10-10.aud.hanno.7590.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 13 songs; 92 min; rated 2.45/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this audience recording barely tolerable in quality, though the jamming itself is solid; Reviewer says recording quality is mediocre and the Going Down The Road jam lacks its own track; Decent audience recording with era-typical hiss, though the music comes through clearly [2][3][5][7][10]

## Around the show

- Guests: false start [1]
- Attendee says several songs are missing from the tape, including a Viola Lee Blues not listed in the setlist [8]
- Attendee recalls Garcia repeating the same three notes at the verse end of Viola Lee Blues for what felt like ages [8]
- Reviewer says the Colden Center was over-supervised and unfriendly to heads by the time they attended Queens College [9]
- Reviewer notes the tape lacks the final songs: Good Lovin', Minglewood Blues, Cumberland Blues and Uncle John's Band [10]
- Ken Lee says he effectively rented the Dead for Judy's 22nd birthday using Queens College student council money [12]
- Attendee claims the band disliked the audience and played only one set, with Garcia visibly irritated [13]
- The last song is not noted in Deadlists and cuts off on the tape after 2:10 [2]
- DeadBase lists Good Lovin', Minglewood, Cumberland and Uncle John's, possibly still on the master [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-10-10.144636.sony-f95.lee.hance.sirmick.flac1648**: taped by Ken and Judy Lee; transferred by Jay Hance and Sirmick; source: Source: Sony F95's > Sony TC124s > Master Cassette (Ampex 361) > Cassette (Maxell XL2S) > DAT(48k) - Recorded by Ken and Judy Lee [1]. Also: Another Ken and Judy Lee recording; Ken posted a review of the show on archive.org [1]
- **gd70-10-10.aud.hanno.7590.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Hanno Bunjes and Ulie Teute; source: Audience [2]. Also: One of the Ken and Judy Lee recordings [12]
